data.G: Initial G remains the supplied baseline; do not select an unmeasured candidate. After research, integrate only correctly validated measured programs, measure any combination rather than assuming gains are additive, and independently confirm the final G under the official protocol.
data.analysis: Choose N=3: the baseline is correct and measures 1.228093878 ms on average over three samples, but its two full-size passes (absolute-value write and scratch read) and three ordered operations offer distinct opportunities. The children separate a hierarchical fused pipeline, a one-kernel atomic alternative, and input-load/reduction tuning so their results can be compared or selectively combined. All candidates must compute from current input for every checked size, overwrite output each call, stay within the supplied scratch buffer, and meet the stated FP64 error bound. No new measurements or source changes were made.

children.objective: Replace the full-size absolute-value intermediate with a two-stage hierarchical sum(abs(x)): the first kernel reads input once and writes one partial per CTA to scratch; the final kernel reduces only those partials and writes output directly. Focus on the pipeline structure and correct handling of small n, not broad load-geometry tuning. Read only initialized partials, fit within scratch, and validate every required size and the FP64 tolerance.
children.subject: Fused hierarchical reduction and scratch traffic

children.objective: Evaluate a distinct single-kernel alternative: reset output in the default stream, stream input once, reduce locally per CTA, then atomicAdd one CTA result to output. Explore keeping CTA atomic count modest; do not rely on scratch initialization or omit the per-call reset. Compare total time including reset and launch overhead against hierarchical candidates, and validate every required size and the FP64 tolerance.
children.subject: Single-kernel CTA aggregation with output atomics

children.objective: Optimize the input streaming and per-CTA reduction mechanics of a two-stage fused partial-sum design, without changing its partial-output/finalizer strategy. Measure suitable contiguous or vectorized loads, multiple accumulators, CTA dimensions, and grid/tile sizes on GH200; handle alignment and tails correctly for every valid input. Judge by full official-call timings and correctness, not kernel-only assumptions.
children.subject: Fused reduction load and launch geometry
